key_insight: A parametric PINN and a tensorial reduced-order model can both learn direct surrogate maps for shallow-water dam-break dynamics, but the PINN becomes much more reliable when shock-aware collocation is added.
engineering_relevance: These models offer fast, non-intrusive alternatives to time-stepping solvers for rapid prediction and parametric studies in shallow-water CFD applications.
method: Parametric physics-informed neural network learns state from space, time, and dam-break parameters.
Non-intrusive tensorial reduced-order model builds a direct reduced surrogate without online time integration.
Shock-aware collocation is introduced to better resolve discontinuities and stabilize the PINN.
evidence_signal: The paper compares both surrogates on out-of-sample and extrapolated parameter values for the 1D shallow-water dam-break problem.
watch_item: Performance may degrade near shocks or under extrapolation if the PINN is not trained with shock-aware sampling.
paper_title: Comparison of a Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network and a Tensorial Reduced-Order Model for the Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem
